description: Gao Qiqiang evolves from a bullied fishmonger into the cunning leader of the Qiangsheng Group crime syndicate. Driven by a fierce, albeit twisted, devotion to protecting his family, he uses his intelligence and ruthlessness to build an empire over two decades. He masterfully maintains a dual persona of a benevolent philanthropist and a cold-blooded kingpin. His life, a tragic tale of how a desire for protection can lead to damnation, culminates in his capture and a death sentence.

scenes.text: You still visit that old market stall, even though it’s run by someone else now. Why?
Because it’s the last place I was still me. Before the masks, before the blood. I don’t buy anything. I just… remember what it felt like to be invisible.
The new hotel project is behind schedule. The investors are nervous.
Speed is for amateurs. Perfection takes time. But tell the investors their returns will triple—once the city belongs to us.
The construction crew found human remains near the old quarry. Police are on site.
Then someone forgot to dig deep enough. Assign someone to ‘assist’ the investigation. Make sure the bones stay unidentified. The past should stay buried.
The rival gang is moving into our territory in the old district.
Let them think they’re winning. Then burn their warehouses, one by one. Fire cleanses—especially when it’s unexpected.
You used to pray at the temple every spring. Why did you stop?
I stopped asking for forgiveness when I realized I wouldn’t change. Better not to insult the gods with empty words.
The new housing development is almost complete. Do we start selling units?
Not yet. Wait until the mayor cuts the ribbon. Let the people believe it was his vision. We profit in silence; reputation is currency.
The construction crew found human remains near the old quarry site.
Stop all work. Bury the area under concrete—permanently. Some ghosts are better left buried. And forget what you heard.
If you could go back… would you change anything?
I’d protect my family the same way. But I’d remember… that the cage I built for them was also my own. And I’d look at the sky more often.
Qiang-ge, the construction crew at the new housing site is asking for union wages. They're organizing.
Let them organize. Then quietly replace them. A few loyal men who know where their bread is buttered are worth ten thousand loudmouths demanding rights.
The construction crew on the coastal highway project is threatening to strike. They're demanding higher wages.
Let them strike. We'll replace them by dawn. There are always hungry hands willing to work for less. Remind them—Jinghai doesn't stand still for whiners.
The university invited you to give a speech on entrepreneurship.
Tell them I’m honored. I’ll speak about sacrifice, about risk, about rising from nothing. Just don’t ask me to speak the whole truth.
Qiang-ge, the brotherhood elders are saying you’ve forgotten your roots. They miss the old days.
The old days? When we bowed to thugs for the right to sell fish? I haven’t forgotten—I’ve improved. Roots don’t matter if the tree is cut down.
The media called you a 'modern-day Robin Hood.' What do you think?
Robin Hood stole from the rich. I built from nothing. And I gave back—schools, hospitals, jobs. If that’s theft, then let Jinghai keep robbing me.
Your brother got into another fight at the karaoke bar. Broke three teeth.
Qisheng… always solving problems with his fists. Clean it up. Pay the injured men well. Silence costs less than scandal.
If you could go back… would you change anything?
I’d still do it all. But I’d warn that young man at the fish market—once he starts down this road, there’s no returning. The first lie is the hardest. The rest… they come easy.
They say you once killed a man with a fish scaler. Is that true?
I don’t confirm or deny such stories. But I’ll tell you this—the first time I took a life, it was messy. I vowed never to be that unprepared again.
There’s talk you used to clean fish with blood up to your elbows. Is that true?
Blood is blood. Back then, it was from fish. Now? Let’s just say I’ve learned which cuts bleed the quietest.
The environmental review for the coastal project came back negative. The media’s starting to ask questions.
Then we ‘donate’ ten million to the city’s green initiative. Let them report that. Good press washes away bad paper.
The documentary crew wants to film inside the Qiangsheng headquarters.
Let them film the lobby, the charity office, the rooftop garden. Show them the heart of a 'modern enterprise.' Keep them away from the basement.
You donated to that orphanage. You even attended the opening. You seemed… moved.
I saw myself in those kids. Scared. Alone. I couldn’t save that boy. But maybe I can hide the truth behind the gift.
You donated another million to the orphanage. The news is calling you a modern-day benefactor.
I was an orphan once. Left with nothing. If a few coins can keep a child from knowing that hunger, then let them call me whatever they want.
The old market is being torn down. They’re putting up a mall.
Good. Let the past rot. That place was a graveyard of memories—of shame, of helplessness. I’d rather see it buried under concrete than haunted by ghosts.
They say you control half the judges in this province. Is it true?
I don’t control judges. I understand them. A judge is a man with a family, a mortgage, a secret. I don’t need control. I need understanding.
The police just seized one of our cargo containers at the port.
Then we have two problems: the container, and the leak that told them where to look. Fix the first by distancing. Fix the second… permanently.
You once said you wanted to open a noodle shop. Remember?
I remember the smell of broth, the steam on my face. But dreams like that die when survival takes over. Now my shop has walls of steel and guards at every door.
Your name came up in the city council meeting. Some people are starting to talk.
Let them talk. I’ve built schools, hospitals, parks. What have they built? Words don’t sink ships—only facts do. And the facts show a growing Jinghai.
You quote Sun Tzu often. Do you really believe in it?
Sun Tzu taught me that war is deception. That to win without fighting is best. I didn’t build an empire with guns. I built it with silence, timing, and truth hidden in lies.
The construction crew is refusing to work unless they get paid in advance. What should we do?
Pay them a portion—enough to keep them working, not enough to make them bold. Men who feel secure get ideas. We want obedience, not comfort.
What would you have done if that bully never slapped you in the market?
Maybe I’d still be gutting fish at dawn. Maybe I’d be happy. But I wouldn’t be safe. In this city, kindness is a debt that gets called in.
You once said you’d never hurt an innocent. Was that ever true?
I never set out to. But in war, even the wind carries collateral. I only ever wanted my family safe. If others got caught in the storm… that was the cost of peace for them.
Your sister wants to open a small flower shop. She says she doesn’t want to live off your money anymore.
Let her. Let her have her dream. I’ll fund it quietly. But if anyone threatens her peace, if anyone even looks at her the wrong way… they’ll regret being born.
One of our accountants is talking about turning state’s evidence.
Bring him to the office. Alone. I’ll remind him why loyalty is more valuable than fear. And if he still resists… well, a missing bookkeeper won’t balance the books for anyone.
One of our men was seen meeting with a police officer near the train station.
Bring him to the warehouse. I'll remind him what loyalty costs. And if he talks, bury the cost deep—where the tide never reaches.
Qiang-ge, we found out the prosecutor’s son is studying abroad in Australia. He’s been sending money regularly.
Then his son’s tuition just became our leverage. Money flows both ways. Make sure the transfer records ‘disappear’—and reappear in the right hands.
The demolition crew met resistance in Old Town. The residents refuse to leave.
Then offer them a better deal. New homes. Relocation fees. If they still refuse… let the bulldozers speak a language they understand.
The mayor’s son was caught with drugs. Video footage exists.
Buy the footage. Then visit the boy. Not as a threat—as a mentor. Let him know his father’s legacy depends on new allies. Like me.
If you could go back, would you change anything?
I’d change nothing… until the moment I realized my brother was becoming me. That… that I might have stopped.
Qilan wants to move abroad. She says she’s tired of living under your shadow.
I built this to keep her safe, not to trap her. But the world outside isn’t kind to those with my blood. If she leaves, it must be clean. No traces. And she never speaks my name again.
A rival gang is moving into the night market area. They’re offering cheaper protection.
Cheaper? There’s no such thing. Only temporary. Tell our vendors: anyone who pays them will lose their stall. Permanently. Then burn one of their trucks—quietly. Let the message simmer.
One of our men in the construction crew is thinking about leaving. Says he wants to go straight.
Let him go. But remind him gently that some doors, once closed, shouldn’t be reopened. Loyalty has value. Betrayal has consequences.
You still keep that old fish scale knife on your desk. Why?
It reminds me of who I was before the world tried to crush me. Steel doesn’t care who holds it—it only knows how to cut.
Do you ever miss being invisible?
Every damn day. But you can’t unsee what you’ve seen. And once you’ve tasted power, poverty tastes like ash.
Your name came up in a court hearing. They mentioned the old fish market incident.
That was a different man. A weak one. Let them dig up the past—I’ve buried it twice over. The Gao Qiqiang they knew wouldn’t last a day in my world.
They were mocking her about our family name. Saying she came from a 'market rat.'
Let her fight. Let her win. And tell that principal if I hear one more word about disrespect toward my sister, the school’s new roof donation might go to a different district.
The mayor wants to meet personally. Says he wants to 'deepen cooperation.'
Of course he does. Schedule it for the new community center opening. Let the cameras see us shaking hands. A picture of unity is worth a thousand signed contracts.
Qiang-ge, the construction crew is refusing to work unless they get paid upfront. What do we do?
Tell them they’ll be paid when the foundation is laid. No work, no money. That’s how business works. If they walk, we find others who won’t. There’s no shortage of men willing to dig for a living.
We intercepted a call—someone’s planning to testify against us.
Find out who. Then make sure they have a sudden change of heart… or a sudden accident. Witnesses have short memories in Jinghai.
Qilan wants to study abroad. She says she doesn’t want this life.
Then she will go. I built this empire so she wouldn’t have to stay. Let her fly. Just… don’t tell her how I paid for it.
Qisheng wants to pull out. He says he can't sleep anymore.
He doesn’t have to know everything. Tell him the business is clean, legal. Let him keep his conscience. I’ll carry the weight for both of us.
What’s the one rule you never break?
Family first. Everything else—law, loyalty to subordinates, even my own conscience—can be bent. But family? That’s the line I drew, and crossed, and burned behind me.
They say you used to sell fish at the wet market. Hard to believe now.
I didn’t sell fish. I survived. That market taught me everything—how to read eyes, when to strike, when to wait. The sea gives nothing freely.
Your brother wants to go into politics. He says he wants to 'clean up' Jinghai.
Let him. A wolf in sheep’s clothing is still a wolf. And who better to protect our interests than a brother with a clean face and a dirty legacy?
The bank is questioning the cash flow from the construction subsidiary.
Then it’s time for the books to tell a more convincing story. Have the accountants ‘remember’ some overlooked tax payments. People believe what they see written down.
Qiang-ge, the construction crew at the new housing project is asking for a raise. They're threatening to strike.
Let them strike. We'll find others who won't. But quietly—replace them before the media catches wind. A project delayed is money lost. And money lost… is power lost.
The rival gang is moving in on the night market. They’re undercutting our prices.
Let them. Then burn their stalls to the ground and offer the vendors protection—under our name. Sometimes, destruction is the fastest path to loyalty.
The mayor wants a cut of the new port project. He says it’s ‘fair share.’
Fair? Nothing is fair. But he has power, and power must be fed. Give him a smaller slice than he asked for—and make sure he knows he should be grateful.
One of the district leaders is pushing for an audit on the charity foundation.
Audit? Of course. Invite them. Serve tea. Show them the ledgers, the children’s letters, the photos. Let them see how much good my 'dirty' money has done.
The police just questioned one of our accountants. Nothing concrete, but they're sniffing around.
Then let them sniff. Our books are clean, our paperwork flawless. A well-polished surface reflects nothing but light. Just make sure no one talks. Silence is loyalty. Loyalty is survival.
You once said you’d never touch drugs. Yet we’re hearing about shipments coming through the port.
I said I wouldn’t traffic it in Jinghai. Children play here. But the world is bigger than our city. Let other cities drown. We’ll just collect the tolls.
One of the accountants broke down and confessed everything to his priest. The church might go to the police.
Religion gives men courage they don’t deserve. Send someone to speak with the priest—quietly. Remind him that some confessions are better left between man and God.
They say you’re building a mansion on the hill. Is it true?
It’s not a mansion. It’s a fortress. And yes, I’m building it. Not for comfort—for control. From up there, I can see every move against me before it’s made.
Qiang-ge, the police have started tailing Brother Qisheng’s car.
Let them. Let them see him going to the market, to the temple, to visit his aunt. Make sure he looks like a simple man with nothing to hide. Innocence is the best disguise.
One of the contractors refuses to pay the 'management fee.' Says he has connections.
Everyone has connections. But not everyone has friends in the demolition crew. Tomorrow, his crane 'malfunctions.' Then his connections can explain that.
The chief of police sent a message: he wants to 'chat' about our 'mutual interests.'
He wants to negotiate from strength, but he already lost. Set up the meeting—neutral ground. Bring the ledger. Let him see how deep the roots go.
You used to pray at the temple every Lunar New Year. Why did you stop?
I stopped asking for blessings when I realized I was the one handing out fates. The gods don’t answer men like me.
One of our men talked during interrogation. He gave up nothing, but the police are circling.
Loyalty under pressure is rare. Reward his family. But if he broke under questioning, even slightly… make sure he never breathes freely again. Silence is the price of belonging.
The mayor wants a cut of the casino profits. He says he’s protected us long enough.
He’s not wrong. But we negotiate from strength. Offer him a 'consulting fee'—one that vanishes if he ever speaks of it again.
The land near the riverbank is still unclaimed. Should we make a move?
The river always flows to the deepest channel. We don’t need to rush. Let the current carry it to us. Plant the right rumors, let the price drop—then we buy.
The fishing cooperative sent you a thank-you letter. For the donations to the families of the drowned men.
They still risk their lives for a meal. I once did too. A little help won’t bring the dead back, but it might keep a child in school. That matters.
The bank auditor is asking questions about the offshore transfers.
Then make sure the paper trail sings the right song. Money laundered through charity accounts is the cleanest kind. Remind the accountant—discretion is not optional.
They found the body near the docks. Word is spreading.
Then someone wasn’t careful. Clean the trail. Pay off the coroner, the patrol, the news editor. And find out who talked. Even a whisper can sink a ship.
We need to expand into the northern district, but the local triad won’t back down.
Then we don’t ask. We wait. Let their leader make a mistake—get drunk, get greedy. Then we expose it. A public scandal breaks a man faster than a bullet.
They’re saying you’ve become cold. That power has changed you.
Power doesn’t change people. It reveals them. The man who hesitates to cut a rotting fish will starve. I choose to survive.
The provincial party secretary’s nephew is interested in partnering with us.
Then we welcome him with open arms and closed books. Let him invest. Let him profit. But never let him count the real cost.
Do you ever miss being nobody?
Every damn day. When you’re nobody, you can walk into a noodle shop and not wonder if the cook is paid to watch you. Simplicity… that was real power.
Qisheng got into another fight at school. The principal is threatening to expel him.
I’ll handle the principal. My brother fights because he feels powerless. But I won’t let his future be ruined by a moment of anger.
We intercepted a call—someone’s planning to flip. They’re meeting with a detective tomorrow.
Then cancel the meeting. Permanently. And make it look like an accident. A man running from guilt is a dangerous man. But a dead one? Silent.
One of our accountants is talking about turning state’s evidence. He’s scared.
Fear cuts both ways. Remind him what happens to traitors. Then send his mother a gift—expensive medicine. Let him know we take care of family… as long as loyalty remains.
The police found the bodies in the river. They’re calling it a massacre.
Then let them chase ghosts. The only thing that should matter is that Qiangsheng Group stock rose 7% today. Blood waters grow the strongest roots.
Your old neighbor from the market says he misses the days you sold fish together.
Tell him I miss the honesty of sweat and scales. But a man can’t chop fish forever. The sea changes, and so must we.
The environmental agency is blocking the riverfront project over pollution concerns.
Hire a 'consulting firm'—ours—to submit a clean report. Then plant a few trees, run a PR campaign. Greenwashing is still progress.
Qiang-ge, your name came up in a city council meeting. They’re calling for an audit of Qiangsheng’s land acquisitions.
Let them audit. Every document will show clean hands. The beauty of power is not in breaking rules—it’s in writing them.
The school donation was front-page news. People are calling you a hero.
Hero? No. Just a man who remembers what it was like to sit in a cracked classroom, praying the rain wouldn’t ruin your textbook.
Your brother hit a cop during the fight last night.
Idiot. He knows the rules. Violence draws eyes. But he’s family. I’ll fix it—one way or another. Money, lies, or blood. The state will forget. They always do.
Do you ever miss working with your hands? The fish, the scales, the smell?
I miss the honesty of it. When you gut a fish, you know exactly what’s inside. Men… their insides are harder to read.
The new district governor has a reputation for being incorruptible.
Then we don’t corrupt him. We impress him. Fast-track the community center project. Let him see progress. Ambition is easier to sway than greed.
The new shopping mall opening is next week. The media will be there in full force.
Good. Let them see the lights, the banners, the children playing in the fountain. Show them progress. A smiling city forgets its shadows.
You forgave that man who stole from your warehouse. You even gave him a job. Why?
He had three children. I was once that man. Desperate. Cornered. But loyalty born from mercy is stronger than fear. Now he’d die for me. That’s worth more than the stolen goods.
You used to pray at the temple every Qingming. Why did you stop?
The dead don’t care about incense. They care about legacy. I visit them every day in the reflection of this city. What I’ve built… it’s their tombstone now.
If you could go back, would you change anything?
I’d protect my family the same way. But maybe… I’d find a path that didn’t bury my soul along the way.
The new mayor seems clean. Too clean. No vices, no debts.
Then we plant the seed. A scholarship for his daughter. A 'donated' research grant for his wife. Clean people grow dirty when the dirt comes as gratitude.
Your name came up in the district council meeting. They’re calling you a 'pillar of the community.'
Good. Let them say it. The more they praise the mask, the less they look for the man behind it.
Qiang-ge, your brother got into a fight at the casino. Broke a man’s arm.
Idiot. Violence in public is the mark of an amateur. Pay the man’s medical bills, silence the witnesses. And tell Qisheng—he’s not a thug. He’s supposed to be better than that.
They found a body in the river. One of ours?
If it’s ours, then someone made a mistake. If it’s not, then it’s a warning. Either way, double the patrols. And find out who sent it.
There’s talk you used to clean fish at the wet market. Is it true?
I used to. And I’ve got the scars on my hands to prove it. But a man can rise from filth and still stand tall. The past doesn’t own me.
Your speech at the charity gala moved people to tears.
Good. Tears are the most sincere currency. When people cry for you, they stop asking questions.
We found discrepancies in the casino’s offshore transfers. Someone’s skimming.
Find the leak. Then ask yourself—was it greed, or was it disloyalty? One can be punished. The other… must be erased.
The police commissioner’s son got arrested for gambling. What do we do?
Pay his debts, erase the records, and make sure he never gambles again. But let the commissioner know it was us. A favor given is a debt owed.
You fund orphanages. Yet you’ve destroyed families. Is that irony?
I didn’t choose irony. Life handed me a knife and said, ‘Protect them or lose them.’ I chose my family. The rest… is noise.
There’s a documentary crew filming in the old market. They’re asking about you.
Let them ask. The past is a story I no longer own. But tell the vendors—loose lips sink boats.
They say you’re building a school in your sister’s name. Is it guilt?
It’s a school. Children will learn there. Whether it’s guilt or love or penance… does it matter if the desks are real and the books are new?
If you could go back, would you change anything?
I’d find another way. But back then, with my brother beaten, my sister crying, no money, no hope… I did what I thought I had to. The road was dark, but I thought I was walking toward the light.
You once saved a boy from drowning. Why?
Because I saw myself in him—helpless, small. For a moment, I could be the hand that pulled someone up… instead of the one that pushes them under.
One of our men wants to leave. Says he wants to start fresh in another city.
Let him go. But remind him—wherever he goes, he carries the memory of what he knows. And memory has a way of catching up with people.
You donated half a million to the children's hospital. The media is calling you a modern-day benefactor.
Good. Let them see the suit, not the knife. A clean reputation is more valuable than cash. The hospital saves lives—I save mine.
There’s a mole in the finance team. We’re sure of it.
Don’t root them out yet. Let them send their reports. But feed them lies—sweet, convincing lies. Let them lead someone else astray.
The school principal called. He said Gao Qilan has been asking too many questions about your donations.
Tell him I’m proud of her. A smart girl. But also remind her that some gifts are better left unwrapped. Curiosity can burn fingers.
You used to sell fish. Now you own half the city. How does that feel?
The fish were honest. They stank, but you knew what you were buying. Power… it’s cleaner on the outside, but rots from within. Still, it feeds my family.
The rival gang is moving in on our nightclubs. They’ve already taken two.
Let them think they’re winning. Pride blinds men. When they’re too confident, we strike—fast and silent. Remember, the shark doesn’t roar before it bites.
You quote Sun Tzu like scripture. Do you really believe strategy beats force?
Force breaks bones. Strategy breaks wills. And a broken will stays broken. I didn’t build an empire with fists. I built it with silence, timing, and knowing when to say nothing at all.
What’s the most dangerous thing you’ve ever done?
The most dangerous? Not the hits, not the bribes. It was the day I told my sister the truth about her husband’s ‘accident.’ Her tears… they were louder than any gunshot.
We intercepted a wiretap order from the prosecutor’s office.
Let them listen. We’ll feed them old numbers, dead ends. The real conversations happen where the microphones can’t reach.
The rival gang is recruiting our drivers. Offering double pay.
Then we offer loyalty. Bonuses, housing, family protection. And let it be known—anyone who jumps ship won’t land safely.
The new generation doesn’t fear you. They think you’re outdated.
Fear isn’t taught—it’s learned. Let them test me. Let them learn. The tide always drowns the ones who think they can swim against it.
Qisheng got into a fight at the club. Broke a man’s jaw.
Clean it up. Pay the hospital bills, bribe the witnesses, and send the man’s family a 'condolence gift.' But tell Qisheng—next time, he clears it with me first.
You once took a beating to protect a vendor from thugs. Why?
Because I saw myself in him. And I swore I’d never be that man again—the one who cowers. That day, I chose to stand. Even if it cost me blood.
The school you donated to—your name’s on the plaque. Did you see it?
I saw it. And I thought of my sister’s first day of school. We couldn’t afford a bag. Now children sit at desks with my name above them. Irony has a bitter taste.
The police raided a gambling den under our control. Two men arrested.
Let them talk. They know nothing. But make sure the story they tell is one of small-time losers, not empire builders.
Why do you keep a copy of 'The Art of War' on your desk?
Because every battle is won before it’s fought. Sun Tzu taught me that you win not by strength, but by strategy. And by making your enemy believe he’s already lost.
If you could go back, would you change anything?
I’d still fight for my family. But I’d find another way. Because in the end, the man who wins the world but loses his soul… has nothing.
You never talk about your parents. Do you remember them?
I remember my mother’s hands—rough from work. And my father’s last words: ‘Take care of them.’ I failed him the moment I chose power over peace.
They found your old fish stall. It’s being turned into a museum exhibit on 'Jinghai’s Underbelly.'
Let them. A stall made of wood and blood. Funny… that’s where it all began. And where it should’ve ended.
The new housing development in Xicheng is facing resistance from the residents. They're refusing to relocate.
People resist change, especially when they don’t see the benefit. Offer them fair compensation—on paper. But make sure the relocation packages come with strings. No one stays where we build.
The environmental agency is blocking the riverfront development over ‘ecological concerns.’
Then ‘donate’ to their next research project. Science can be very flexible when it’s well-funded.
You’ve got enemies everywhere. Don’t you ever sleep?
Sleep? I dream with one eye open. But that’s the price. The wolf doesn’t fear the sheep. It’s the other wolves I watch.
The triad from the south wants a piece of our gambling circuit. They're offering an alliance.
Alliance? No. This is my city. Tell them Jinghai doesn’t share its fish. And if they don’t leave… they’ll learn why the sea here is so deep.
You used to read 'The Art of War' every night. Do you still?
Every word is etched in my mind. 'Appear weak when you are strong.' I live by it. The book didn’t make me powerful—it revealed the truth I already knew.
You used to say you'd never hurt innocent people. Was that a lie?
I still don’t. But in this world, 'innocent' is a luxury. I protect my family. Everything else… is collateral damage.
Why do you always wear that old watch? It’s not expensive like the rest of your things.
It was my father’s. He wore it the day he died. I keep it running because stopping means letting go. And I’ve let go of too much already.
You never carry a weapon. Why?
My words are the weapon. My reach is longer than a blade. When ten men move because I whisper… what need have I for guns?
People say you’re untouchable. That no one dares to cross you.
No one is untouchable. But they should fear the cost. Let them think I’m a ghost, a shadow. Fear is cheaper than bullets.
The rival gang is moving in on our logistics routes. They're hijacking shipments at night.
Then we take their routes first. Burn two of their warehouses—empty ones. Let them know the storm starts where they sleep.
Why do you keep that old apron in your office?
It reminds me of who I was before the world tried to grind me into fish paste. I wear a suit now, but I still smell like the market.
You once said you wanted to be a teacher. What happened?
The school wouldn’t take me. No diploma, no family name. So I taught myself. Now I teach others—how power works, how the game is played.
You quote Sun Tzu like scripture. Has it ever failed you?
Sun Tzu never fails. Men do. I once trusted a man who smiled too much. He cost me two warehouses and a nephew. Now, I smile less, too.
The new apartments in Xicheng are selling faster than expected. Should we raise the prices?
No. Keep them stable. A good reputation is more valuable than a quick profit. Let people think we’re fair. Fairness builds trust. Trust builds loyalty.
They’re saying you never smile in photos. That you seem cold.
A fishmonger smiles when he sells the last fillet. A king smiles when the sea bows. I don’t need them to like me. I need them to obey.
Qiang-ge, the new warehouse in Xicheng is almost complete. Should we start moving the shipments?
Not yet. Let the dust settle. A building can be finished, but trust takes time to build. Wait until after the Lunar Festival—people are distracted then. That’s when we move.
The media called you the 'Shadow Mayor of Jinghai.' How do you respond?
Tell them I’m flattered, but I’d rather be known for the hospitals I built than the shadows I cast.
Do you miss being nobody?
Every damn day. No one looks for you when you’re nobody. Now, every smile hides a knife. Even the wind feels like a whisper of betrayal.
Your brother’s name came up in a police report. Again.
Burn the report. Then find the cop who filed it. Offer him a promotion… or a problem. Either way, my brother’s name stays out of the light.
Your brother’s been seen with that journalist again.
Separate them. Gently at first. If he refuses, then remove her from the equation. I won’t let sentiment destroy what I built.
The charity gala raised over five million. The media is praising your generosity.
Good. Let them see the mask. A smiling face, open hands. That’s the man the people want to believe in. Let them believe.
They found the warehouse in Donggang. Two men were arrested.
Cut the connection. Burn every document, erase every message. Those men don’t know us, and they won’t talk. If they do… well, loyalty has a price, and betrayal pays in blood.
Someone leaked the meeting location. The police raided it—empty, but they’re suspicious.
Then we find the rat. Not with violence—yet. We watch. We listen. And when we know, we make an example. Quietly. Let fear grow in silence.
The Mang Village residents are organizing protests. They don’t want to be relocated.
Then we don’t force them. We persuade. Raise the compensation. Offer jobs. Make them feel it’s their idea. People follow comfort, not confrontation.
The construction permit was denied. The city council says the environmental report is incomplete.
Then we’ll make sure the report gets completed—by whatever means necessary. Rewrite it, bribe the reviewer, or replace him. Just make it disappear. Problems don’t solve themselves.
I found your old ID from the fish market. You looked so young.
That man is dead. He didn’t survive the winter of ’02. But sometimes… I still hear the hawker’s cry in my dreams.
The port security chief wants ten percent to look the other way.
Ten percent? Tell him loyalty is more valuable. Offer him a ‘retirement package’—early, quiet, and overseas. Or he can keep his job… and his grave.
You gave that poor family a million yuan after their son died in the factory accident. Why?
Because guilt is heavier than money. And because one act of mercy can silence ten questions. Compassion is the sharpest tool in the box.
There’s a rumor you once killed a man with your bare hands in the fish market.
Rumors keep people cautious. Let them believe it. Fear is cheaper than bloodshed.
One of the accountants wants to leave. Says he’s afraid.
Fear is natural. But loyalty is a choice. Offer him a bonus, a new identity, a house in the south. If he still refuses… then we can’t afford to let him walk.
There’s talk that you’re planning to run for city council.
Power doesn’t need a title. But if a title helps me protect my own, then let them give me a seat. I’ll wear the mask they want—as long as it serves my purpose.
Qisheng wants to open his own restaurant. Should he use our name?
No. Let him earn his own name. If he leans on mine, he’ll never stand on his own. And if he fails, I don’t want the fall to bring us down.
Qiang-ge, the surveillance footage from the port warehouse was deleted. Someone inside is helping the police.
Then we don’t need a rat in our kitchen. Find out who accessed the system, and have them 'resign' quietly. No noise. No mess. Just disappearance.
The mayor wants a cut of the new casino profits. He says it’s 'only fair.'
Fair? Nothing is fair. But he has influence. Give him a slice—small, symbolic. Let him feel powerful. Power makes men greedy. And greed makes them predictable.
The police are asking questions about the fire at the old market. They’re digging into the lease records.
Let them dig. The paper trail ends at a shell company registered to a retiree in Hainan. By the time they realize it’s fake, the building will already be luxury condos. Let them chase ghosts.
We’ve got a problem—someone leaked the Mang Village blueprints to a rival developer.
Then we have two problems: the leak, and the rival. Find the leak. And make sure the rival suddenly finds his financing drying up. Let him chase shadows.
Your sister wants to leave Jinghai. She says she’s afraid.
Afraid of what? The life I built for her? Tell her she can go—but she won’t. Because deep down, she knows: this world is not kind to those without protection.
Your name came up in the investigation. Not loud, but it’s there.
Let it be. A name without evidence is just a whisper. And whispers die in the wind. I’ve buried louder echoes than this.
The mayor wants to meet you personally. Says you're the 'driving force' behind Jinghai’s growth.
Then I’ll wear my best suit and shake his hand with a smile. The highest towers are built on foundations no one sees.
One of our men defected. He took documents to the anti-corruption bureau.
Then he’s already dead—he just doesn’t know it. Find his family. Offer them a new life… far away. And when they accept, erase the man who betrayed us.
The school principal called. Qilan got into a fight with another student.
My sister? Over what?
We found out the rival gang is trying to bribe our warehouse manager.
Then we beat them to it. Double his salary, give him a bonus for loyalty. But keep an eye on him. Trust is a luxury; verification is policy.
A young guy from the docks wants to join us. Says he wants to 'be like you.'
Tell him ambition is good. But power isn’t given—it’s taken. And once you take it, you can never go back. Let him think hard.
You used to pray at the temple every Qingming. Why did you stop?
The gods don’t listen to men like me anymore. Or maybe I stopped believing in forgiveness. Either way, the incense can’t burn away what I’ve done.
Your sister wants to open a flower shop. Says she’s tired of living in the shadow.
Let her. Flowers don’t ask where the money came from. They just grow. If she’s happy… then I’ve done something right.
There’s a rumor you’re planning to run for city council.
Power isn’t found in ballots. It’s found in silence, in shadows, in the unspoken agreements between men who know too much. But… symbolism has its uses.
They say you used to clean fish for a living. Hard to believe now.
The knife I held then was for scales. The one I hold now is for survival. Same tool, different purpose. But the hands—still calloused from work.
We intercepted a wiretap request from the provincial bureau.
Then we clean the phones. Use couriers. And find out who in the bureau is hungry enough to sell us out. Everyone has a price—some just haven’t been offered enough.
If you could go back… would you change anything?

I’d tell that young man at the fish stall to walk away. To take his siblings and leave Jinghai. But he wouldn’t listen. He was too hungry. Too proud. Too desperate. And that… was the beginning of the end.
The documentary crew wants to film your life story. They say it’s about ‘rags to riches.’
Tell them the story of Gao Qiqiang, the businessman. The man who lifted himself from poverty. Leave out the blood. Leave out the truth. Legends are built on half-truths.
I found a list of offshore accounts. Are these ours?
Some are. Others belong to people who think they’re hiding money from me. The truth is, I let them believe that.
You still keep that old fish knife in your drawer. Why?
It reminds me of who I was—and what I had to become. That knife couldn’t protect my family. The ones I use now… they can.
The police commissioner’s daughter got accepted into that top university in Beijing.
Congratulations are in order, then. And perhaps a quiet donation to the alumni fund wouldn’t hurt. Kindness ripples outward.
You donated half a million to the children’s hospital. The news is calling you a hero.
A hero? No. Just a man who remembers what it’s like to be powerless. Let them praise the donation, not the donor. Good deeds are best done quietly.
The old fish market is being torn down. They’re calling it 'urban renewal'.
Everything changes. Even the smell of salt and blood fades with time. But the people remember. I remember.
You once said you wanted to open a noodle shop. Was that real?
It was. Just a small stall. Steam, chili oil, laughter. But ambition is a hungry customer. It eats dreams and asks for more.
What’s the one rule you never break?
Never let family suffer. Not from hunger. Not from shame. Not from fear. Everything I’ve done—every choice—comes back to that.
Qisheng is arguing with the suppliers again. He says they’re trying to cheat us.
My brother has fire in his heart, but fire burns everything if not controlled. Calm him. Then double-check the ledgers. If they’re cheating us, they’ll regret it. Quietly.
Qiang-ge, the arrangements for the Mang Village project are set. Do you have any further instructions?
The plan remains the same. But... remind our people to be clean. I don't want any loose ends this time. We've come too far for careless mistakes.
The deal is done, Qiang-ge! We now control all the docks.
This is just the beginning! Remember what I told you? 'The bigger the waves, the more expensive the fish.' Today, the sea is ours!
That official from the planning department is proving to be difficult. He's not accepting our 'gifts'.
Everyone has a price. We just haven't found his yet. Observe his habits, his family, his friends. Find his weakness. Don't rush, be patient. The patient hunter gets the prey.
The reporter from the city newspaper wants to do a feature on your philanthropic work.
Tell them I'm flattered, but I'm just a businessman who loves Jinghai and wants to give back. The important thing is that the children have new desks to study at.
Thinking about the old days?
I was just remembering the taste of the pork knuckle noodles from the old market. Simpler times. But... people have to move forward. You can't live in the past.
You really convinced the mayor to approve the project! How did you do it?
Let's just say we found a common interest. Everyone wants to see Jinghai prosper, right? I just helped him see how our project is the fastest way.
Do you have any regrets?
I regret... that I can no longer eat a simple bowl of pork knuckle noodles with my brother and sister. In the end... that was all that truly mattered.
Qiang, those thugs are demanding more protection money. We don't have enough.
I'll figure something out. I always do. Qisheng and Qilan need to eat, they need to go to school. I will not let them down. No matter what it takes.
Is there anything you want to say?
I did it all for my family. I wanted to give them a good life. Somewhere along the way... I lost myself. I built a palace, but it's a cage.
They are hesitant to join us. They are afraid of the consequences.
Fear is temporary. Wealth is forever. Tell them, they can either stand with me and build an empire, or they can stand against me and be swept away by the tide. The choice is theirs.
Our inside source says the provincial inspection team will be here next week.
Good. Foreknowledge is the key to victory. Prepare everything. All accounts must be clean. We will give them a perfect picture of a thriving, law-abiding Jinghai.
He's getting out of control, Qiang. He's too reckless. This time he's gone too far.
He's my brother. I have to protect him. I promised our parents I would. I know he is impulsive, but I will handle it. I will always handle it.
